title: Slano, Croatia Cost Guide 2027: Daily Budgets & Prices

content:
## How Much Does Slano Cost in 2027?

Slano is a small harbor town of the Dubrovnik Riviera, about 35 km northwest of Dubrovnik. Prices run clearly below Dubrovnik's Old Town and below Cavtat, mainly because accommodation is mostly family-run apartments and the dining scene is small. Costs rise sharply in July and August. The figures below are typical ranges for the peak summer season. Spring and autumn are cheaper.

## Daily Budget by Travel Style

| Style | Per person, per day | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| Budget | €70–€100 | Shared apartment, groceries, one cheap restaurant meal, local bus |
| Mid-range | €120–€180 | Private apartment or 3-star room, two restaurant meals, a boat trip or day trip |
| Comfort | €200–€300+ | 4–5-star hotel, restaurant dinners, rental car, excursions |

These figures assume two people sharing a room. Solo travelers pay close to the full room price, so their per-person costs rise by 30–50%.

## Accommodation Costs in Slano

### Apartments and guesthouses

Private apartments and guesthouses make up most of the supply. In summer, a double typically costs €60–€115 per night. Properties such as Apartment Gabrijela, Guest House Pavković, Apartments Vila Riva and Vila Mozara sit in this band. Listings with a sea view, a pool or a location within 100 m of the beach sit at the top of it. Minimum stays of 3–7 nights are common in July and August. Many hosts charge a tourist tax on top of the room rate, so check whether the quoted price includes it.

### Hotels

Average nightly rates for 3-star hotels are around €70 in the shoulder season, rising to €110–€140 at peak. Two larger hotels dominate the upper end:

- **Hotel Osmine** is a 4-star seafront hotel on Grgurići Bay with a private beach, a seasonal pool and a restaurant. Summer rates for two people generally start around €115–€230.
- **Admiral Grand Hotel** is a 5-star property with rooms starting near €190–€260 in high season. Prices at the hotel bar are not low: a large sandwich is €11, a tuna salad €13, a draft beer €5.50 and a cola €4.

Five-star rooms in Slano start at around €200, far below Dubrovnik's prices for the same category. That is the main reason to choose Slano as a luxury base.

### When to book

The cheapest rooms appear in May, early June, and September to early October. Book summer rooms at least 2–3 months ahead, because the small number of apartments sells out for August. Opinionated take: most visitors overspend on hotels here. A well-reviewed apartment at €80–€100 gives you a kitchen and a balcony and beats a €200 hotel room, given how small and quiet the town is.

## Food and Drink Prices

Slano has a modest restaurant scene along the harbor and in the bay. Konoba-style seafood places and pizzerias serve most visitors. Restaurant Kolarin (seafood) and Trattoria Pizzeria Lavanda (Italian) are both within a couple of minutes' walk of the center.

| Item | Typical price |
|---|---|
| Pizza or pasta | €10–€16 |
| Grilled fish (per portion) | €22–€40 |
| Seafood main course, restaurant | €18–€30 |
| Draft beer (0.5 l) | €4.50–€6 |
| Coffee | €1.80–€3 |
| Bakery snack or burek | €2–€4 |

A full restaurant dinner for two with wine runs roughly €60–€100. Self-catering lowers daily food costs to around €15–€25 per person. A grocery shop sits near the harbor, and Ston and Dubrovnik have larger supermarkets.

### Food savings tips

- Order fresh fish by weight only after asking the per-kilo price. Fish is the item that most often inflates a bill.
- Eat the main meal at lunch, when many places offer cheaper set dishes.
- Buy local wine, olive oil and Ston oysters directly from producers in nearby Mali Ston and Ston instead of in tourist shops.

## Getting There and Getting Around

### Bus

Slano is on the coastal road between Dubrovnik and Ston. A one-way bus ticket to Dubrovnik starts at about €5–€6. Journeys take about 35–45 minutes, covering roughly 22–30 km depending on routing. The local line 12 bus run by Libertas serves the route, and intercity operators such as FlixBus add several departures daily, from the early morning to about 22:00. Timetables thin out on Sundays and in winter, so check them the day before.

### Car and parking

The drive to Dubrovnik takes about 35 minutes. Fuel for a round trip costs roughly €6–€10. Most apartments in Slano include free parking, which is a real saving compared with Dubrovnik. Parking in Dubrovnik is expensive, so use the bus for Old Town day trips and keep the car for Ston and the peninsula.

### Taxi and transfers

A taxi from Dubrovnik Airport to Slano costs far more than the bus, typically €70–€100 each way. Pre-booked transfers are often cheaper than metered taxis and give you a fixed price.

## Things to Do and What They Cost

Much of Slano is free. The pebble beaches in town and at Grgurići Bay cost nothing, and the harbor promenade and the Franciscan monastery church of St. Jerome are open to walk around without a fee.

- **Beaches:** free, except at hotel-run areas where sunbeds cost around €10–€25 per set.
- **Ston Walls:** about 20 km away. Entry is a ticket fee of around €10–€15 in season. Check current prices and the closing time before you go.
- **Oysters in Mali Ston:** a half-dozen costs roughly €10–€15 at a local restaurant.
- **Kayak or boat hire:** around €15–€30 per hour for kayaks, with half-day boat trips costing more.
- **Day trip to Dubrovnik:** about €10–€12 for a return bus, plus entry fees for the Old Town walls, which are among the most expensive attractions in the region.

## Money-Saving Tips for Slano

1. **Travel in shoulder season.** June and September give warm sea water and noticeably lower room rates than August.
2. **Pick an apartment with a kitchen.** Cooking breakfast and some dinners cuts the food bill by roughly half.
3. **Stay outside the center.** Properties 500–800 m back from the harbor are often €10–€20 cheaper per night and still a short walk from the beach.
4. **Use the bus for Dubrovnik.** It avoids Old Town parking fees and costs less than fuel plus parking.
5. **Carry some cash.** Small family-run apartments and konobas sometimes prefer cash or add a card fee, so keep a few hundred euros in cash.

## Sample Budgets for 3 Days in Slano

- **Budget traveler:** about €220–€300 total per person, with an apartment shared by two, groceries, one dinner out and a Dubrovnik bus trip.
- **Mid-range couple:** about €700–€1,000 total for two, with a sea-view apartment, restaurant meals each day, and a trip to Ston.
- **Comfort couple:** about €1,200–€1,800 total for two in a 4–5-star hotel with dinners, a rental car and excursions.

Prices are estimates for the peak season and vary by date, so treat them as a planning range and confirm the final rate when booking.

faq.question: Is Slano expensive?
faq.answer: No. Slano is cheaper than Dubrovnik and Cavtat, with apartments from about €60–€115 per night in summer. Five-star rooms start at around €200, well below Dubrovnik's prices for similar hotels.

faq.question: How much money do I need per day in Slano?
faq.answer: Budget travelers need about €70–€100 per person per day, and mid-range travelers €120–€180. The largest cost is accommodation, followed by restaurant meals.

faq.question: How much is the bus from Slano to Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: A one-way ticket starts at about €5–€6. The trip takes roughly 35–45 minutes, and several buses run daily, with the last departures in the evening.

faq.question: What is the cheapest time to visit Slano?
faq.answer: May, June, September and early October offer the lowest rates, with warm weather and more availability. July and August are the most expensive and often have minimum stays.

faq.question: How much does a meal cost in Slano?
faq.answer: Pizza or pasta costs about €10–€16, and a seafood main course about €18–€30. A dinner for two with wine typically costs €60–€100.

faq.question: Do I need a car in Slano?
faq.answer: Not strictly, because buses connect Slano with Dubrovnik and Ston. A car is useful for the Pelješac peninsula and Ston, and most apartments in Slano offer free parking.

faq.question: Can I pay by card in Slano?
faq.answer: Hotels, larger restaurants and shops accept cards. Some small apartments and konobas prefer cash, so keep some euros on hand.

quickAnswer: Slano is one of the cheaper stops on the Dubrovnik Riviera. Budget travelers can manage on about €70–€100 per person per day. Mid-range visitors should expect €120–€180. Private rooms and apartments start around €60–€115 a night in summer. Five-star hotel rooms start near €200, and the bus to Dubrovnik costs about €5.
